changePolicy.r2AuthoritativeShape: R2 is a polarity/completeness pair for mathematical-result records. Legacy R2 concept IDs resolve for migration only and are not valid new assignments.
changePolicy.r3Cardinality: multi-valued; a primary value is a browsing convenience, not a claim that other forms are subordinate
changePolicy.r4Admission: A candidate remains hidden from browse until two distinct source-backed result uses and vocabulary review make it stable.

polarity.definition: The result establishes an affirmative answer or direction; completeness is coded separately.
The result establishes a negative answer or counterexample direction; completeness is coded separately.
The result establishes an impossibility or undecidability direction; completeness is coded separately.

completeness.definition: The anchor claim is resolved in its complete tracked scope.
A documented quantitative or algorithmic frontier is improved without a matching endpoint.
A material subcase, direction or conditional version is established without settling or moving a quantified frontier.

r2Dimensions.combinationRule: Polarity and completeness are independent; every polarity may be paired with settled, frontier_moved or partial when supported.
r2Dimensions.constructionRule: Construction and witness information is coded only in R3.

concepts.definition: A new theorem, counterexample, construction, exact computation, bound, algorithmic guarantee or classification is the principal contribution.
Encoding and machine-checking mathematical content or building reusable formal infrastructure is the principal contribution.
A reusable AI, search, computation or formalisation system is the principal contribution.
Capability measurement or system comparison on a defined mathematical task set is the principal contribution.
Existing evidence is organised, reviewed or quantitatively mapped without a new target theorem as the main contribution.
A stated target or implication is proved in its intended scope.
A conjecture, universal assertion or proposed implication is disproved.
A decision, approximation or construction task is shown impossible under stated assumptions.
A meaningful case, direction or conditional result is established without settling the target.
A previous numerical, asymptotic or extremal bound is strengthened but not shown sharp.
A complexity, approximation or resource guarantee is improved without a matching optimality result.
The main contribution is an explicit or existential mathematical object.
A quantity is determined exactly, or all objects in the stated class are characterised.
An existing or newly produced mathematical result is encoded and checked in a proof assistant.
Reusable definitions, lemmas or interfaces are the primary contribution.
A reusable AI, search or formalisation system is introduced or materially extended.
Systems are compared on a defined set of mathematical tasks.
Prior work is organised, reviewed or quantitatively mapped without a new target theorem.
Establishes the target without making negation of the conclusion the organising strategy.
Uses an assumed negation of the target as the principal global strategy.
Refutes a universal assertion by providing an object satisfying the assumptions and violating the conclusion.
Establishes existence through a construction, including long recursive or prescribed-object constructions.
Establishes existence without producing a usable witness or construction procedure.
Converts the target to an equivalent or sufficient condition that can be resolved.
Uses induction, structural recursion, transfinite recursion or a related iterative construction as a principal method.
Uses random choice or a probabilistic estimate to establish existence.
Proves a finite claim by complete enumeration of the relevant search space.
Produces a result whose correctness is checked by a separate deterministic verifier or certificate checker.
Search directly produces a proof term or script accepted by a formal prover.
Reports computational or empirical support that does not establish the mathematical claim as a theorem.
Redistributes a conserved combinatorial charge according to local rules to rule out all minimal counterexamples.
Uses Razborov's flag-algebra framework to convert asymptotic density constraints into semidefinite inequalities.
Constructs a local or topological algebraic object while controlling its completion to a specified target.
Controls generic formal fibres in a completion or local-ring construction to obtain the required prime-spectrum behaviour.
Encodes combinatorial or geometric information in polynomials and derives the target from their algebraic properties.
Translates the mathematical constraints into Boolean satisfiability for search or certified unsatisfiability checking.
Uses a feasible dual solution as a checkable certificate for a linear-programming bound.
Defines objects along a well-order beyond the finite ordinals, using earlier stages to construct each successor or limit stage.

legacyR2Mappings.note: Construction is an R3 argument form, not an R2 outcome.
Code settled_yes/settled only when the tracked anchor is completely answered; otherwise use frontier_moved or partial.

changePolicy.p1SourceClaimed: sourceClaimed is a separate boolean evidence qualifier for a matching source attribution, not a fourth allocation mode. A conflicting source attribution remains in migration notes.
changePolicy.p1Precedence: Use the conservative human-led label unless concrete operations and cited evidence make the decisive generation stage reconstructible; a bare boolean or source claim is insufficient. Use an explicit missing state when even human-led allocation is unsupported.
changePolicy.note: P1–P4 are independent production dimensions, not one parent–child path. P1 is always accompanied by the Minimal generation/checking/write-up stage table.

concepts.definition: Humans own the principal strategy or proof; AI may supply bounded assistance such as search, examples, algebra, checking or editing.
Humans and systems make interdependent substantive contributions at the decisive mathematical stage, with neither cleanly described as merely assisting.

The system supplies the decisive search, strategy, proof or construction; humans may select, prompt, curate, edit or validate without materially supplying that decisive step. The generation-stage evidence must be reconstructible.

A source explicitly reports no substantive human intervention during the named decisive mathematical stage, and the record preserves a supporting quotation or precise source location. This legacy attribution does not by itself establish the active AI-led code and is never treated as a reviewed project-wide fact.
A comparison or verification artifact is produced without AI involvement.
The available sources do not support a defensible allocation of substantive work.
The substantive reasoning is represented primarily in informal mathematical language.
Executable programs, symbolic computation or generated code carry the substantive search or reasoning.
The substantive reasoning is represented as formal definitions and proof terms or scripts checked by a prover.
Informal mathematical reasoning is translated into, repaired against or paired with a formal proof representation.
Computation or search produces an object or certificate subsequently checked in a formal or independently specified checker.
Multiple representations are used without a defensible primary representation, or the representation is not reported.
One or more bounded prompts without an autonomous iterative controller.
One agent plans or revises across multiple steps using feedback or tools.
Distinct agents or contexts have specialised roles such as planning, generation, criticism or formal proving.
Candidate programs or mathematical objects are generated, evaluated and selected over repeated generations.
A learned component is coupled to a symbolic deduction, constraint or proof engine.
Distinct informal, computational or formal systems operate in a defined sequence.
The workflow retrieves mathematical statements, literature, library lemmas or examples during the run.
A critic gives qualitative feedback to a generator.
A verifier applies a defined acceptance check and returns repair feedback or a pass/fail decision.
A controller constructs or revises subgoals, modules or proof obligations.
State survives context compression, sessions or independent agent calls.
Multiple candidate proofs, programs or obligations are explored concurrently.
Human approval, selection, hints or corrections occur at recorded intervention points.

legacyMappings.label: Source-claimed autonomous
legacyMappings.note: Use AI-led only when concrete, cited generation-stage operations reconstruct the decisive allocation; otherwise use the conservative active mode and retain the source attribution in migration notes.

legacyMappings.label: Human-only control
legacyMappings.note: Human-only controls belong in verification or comparison metadata, not the result-production P1 summary.

legacyMappings.label: Architecture not reported
legacyMappings.note: Store the explicit state, not a concept ID.

changePolicy.replayField: Every record and every event states replayedHere explicitly; source-reported execution is not replay here.
changePolicy.correspondenceRule: Every kernel or certificate event requires an assessed statement relation. Unknown is allowed but blocks formally_verified.
changePolicy.formalAssuranceRule: formally_verified requires a contributing passed kernel event with complete_claim scope and equivalent or stronger statement correspondence.
changePolicy.note: Families and methods describe what happened. Assurance summaries, if shown, are lossy derived labels and never replace events.

concepts.definition: A check performed inside the originating model workflow or team with limited independence.
A person reviews a specified scope of the mathematics or its correspondence to an intended claim.
Executable tests, symbolic calculations, numerical checks or finite enumeration check a specified scope.
A compact artifact is checked against an independently specified checker or verification condition.
A proof assistant or formal comparison process checks a precisely represented statement.
A party independent of the originating workflow replays or independently establishes the claim.
A venue process or publication status is recorded separately from mathematical, computational and formal checks.
A model or agent judges its own output; useful feedback but minimal independence.
Another model checks the output; independence depends on harness, data and team.
A qualified person checks a stated scope of the mathematics; identity, procedure and independence are recorded where known.
Code passes specified tests; this establishes only the tested behaviour.
Symbolic or numerical calculations support stated identities or cases.
All cases in a defined finite space are checked.
A small or independently checkable artifact establishes the result relative to checker correctness.
The formal theorem is accepted relative to its definitions, imports and allowed axioms.
aliases: Lean check with trusted native computation

concepts.definition: A human or comparison tool checks that the formal statement represents the intended informal claim, including any weakened scope or altered assumptions.
A different party reruns supplied artifacts in a supplied or equivalent environment.
A different party establishes the claim using independently created artifacts or a new proof or formalisation.
The work has passed a venue process; this does not by itself establish mathematical or formal correctness.

legacyMappings.label: Published prior result
legacyMappings.note: This records reliance on prior literature, not verification of the new result; retain it as source-role metadata unless a specific verification event is documented.

changePolicy.classificationScope: Searchable system metadata, not a browse-facet hierarchy.
changePolicy.matchingRule: Prefer explicit source attribution. Aliases support deterministic matching but never infer an exact snapshot, role or configuration. Mixed families must be recorded when one displayed label intentionally represents more than one provider family.

concepts.definition: OpenAI model and agent products, including GPT-branded models and Codex.
Anthropic Claude models and Claude Code.
Google and Google DeepMind model or proof systems, including Gemini and AlphaProof.
Lean proof-assistant environments and the Mathlib library.
Isabelle proof-assistant environments, including Isabelle/HOL.
The Rethlas mathematical discovery workflow and Matlas retrieval component.
The Aletheia mathematical reasoning or formal proof system family.
A single displayed system entry intentionally combines models from more than one provider family and cannot be split from the available evidence.
A system is identified, but the available family registry does not yet provide a defensible family assignment.
